fields.h1: Build a Work Order Form That Carries Each Job to Sign-Off
fields.hero_description: Get a work order form that sends each repair to the right technician and closes it on site with the parts used and a signature.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Handles After Submit
fields.features_subheading: A paper form records the request. These six pieces keep the job moving until someone signs it off.
fields.feature_1:
Priority set by the type of problem

Tag categories like water leak or no heat as urgent. Those requests skip the queue and reach whoever is on call, while a sticky closet door waits for the next scheduled visit.
fields.feature_2:
Photos and access notes up front

Ask for a close-up photo of the problem and whether a technician may enter when nobody is home. The tech arrives knowing which part to bring and which door to knock on first.
fields.feature_3:
Routing to the shop that does the work

Send each request to a trade queue based on its category, such as electrical or plumbing. Each supervisor sees one queue of their own, with the most urgent jobs at the top.
fields.feature_4:
Close-out fields filled at the job

Log labor hours and parts from a phone on site, with a note on what was fixed. The requester signs on the screen, and the order stays open until every required field has a value.
fields.feature_5:
Status emails for the person who asked

Email the requester whenever the status changes, with the assigned shop and the scheduled date. The front desk stops fielding calls about whether anyone saw the request at all.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can extend

Export the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans when you want to link the form to an asset register or host the app on your own infrastructure. The code is yours to modify.

fields.usecase_heading: Work Orders for Four Kinds of Crews
fields.tab_content_1:
Water leaks reach the on-call tech in one step

A tenant in Unit 3B at Alder Court Apartments reports a water leak from a phone, with a photo of the ceiling and permission to enter. Leaks and no-heat calls go to Marcus, the on-call technician, as a Slack message with the photo. Everything else joins the weekly queue for that building.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every request lands in its trade shop queue

Ridgeview College runs one link for every building on campus. Staff choose a room and a category, and the request goes to the matching trade shop. The requester gets an email when the shop assigns it and again when the job is marked done. Supervisors work only their own queue.
fields.tab_content_3:
Closed on site with a signature and an invoice

On the last job of the day, a Lumen Heating technician logs 2.5 hours of labor at $110 an hour, plus a capacitor at $48 and a contactor at $36. The homeowner signs on the phone screen. Closing the work order creates a $359 invoice in QuickBooks with every line copied over.
fields.tab_content_4:
A drywall order over budget waits for the PM

Harbor Line Construction issues work orders to subcontractors with a not-to-exceed amount. The Elm Street drywall budget is $42,000, and $38,900 is already committed. A new $4,800 order for Level 3 would reach $43,700, and it waits for the project manager.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Work Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan the routing and close-out rules for a work order form before Emergent builds it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the person who fixes it
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the categories that set routing
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set a limit that needs approval
fields.howto_step_1_des: Note what a technician asks before leaving the shop: where the job is and what is wrong. A photo answers the second question better than any description. Every field on the form should save the tech a phone call.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the three or four categories the work splits into, such as electrical and plumbing. Each category maps to one shop or one person. No request sits in a shared inbox waiting for someone to claim it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write one line on which problems count as urgent and who hears about them after hours. Water leaks and failed heating in winter are common choices. Name a person for each night of the week, weekends included.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which jobs need a sign-off before work starts. A dollar threshold is the simplest rule: anything estimated above it goes to a manager, and smaller jobs are assigned straight away. Write down who approves when that manager is out.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your fields and rules into one prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the request form and a work orders table behind it, with a queue for each shop. Change a rule later the same way, by asking for it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: List what a technician records to finish a job, such as labor hours and parts with their prices. Add a signature field and mark which fields must be filled before the order closes. Connect QuickBooks or Xero if closed jobs become invoices.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 File a test request from a hallway
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the form on a phone and file a fake urgent request from a hallway. Confirm the alert arrives, then close the order as the technician would. Check that the row in the table matches what you entered.

claims_to_source: A purchase order authorizes buying goods or services from a vendor, while a work order authorizes and describes a job to be done
A work request is submitted by the person who needs the work; it becomes a work order once it is approved and assigned
A maintenance work order describes a maintenance task, who does it and when, and records the labor and parts used
Closing out a work order means adding the labor hours and completion notes before changing its status to closed
